$description: LC brand tokens, the one source of truth. Edit this file, then run: python3 tokens/build_tokens.py (it writes tokens/tokens.css and step3/tokens.html, and stops if a colour pair fails its contrast check).

tierra-suave.$description: Secondary text: subtitles, captions, footers. Google Slides cannot fade text, so this is a solid colour.

selva.$description: Lines on light backgrounds. Dark backgrounds.

barro.$description: The dot. Accents. Spanish lines on light backgrounds.

barro-claro.$description: Lines on dark backgrounds. On Selva, large text only.

cielo.$description: Spanish lines and small labels on dark backgrounds.

pairs.use: Spanish lines and accents on sand
Spanish lines and small labels on dark green
Large text only on dark green (18 pt, or 14 pt bold, and up)
Spanish lines and accents on document pages

mono.use: Small labels, in capitals: page numbers, section labels, ¡Hola, hola!

font.$note: lineBox: the font's ascent plus descent as a share of its size, which Google Docs uses as single line spacing (measured from Google's PDF export, 1 Oct 2026: Encode Sans and Encode Sans Expanded 1.25, JetBrains Mono 1.32).

slides.$description: Google Slides and Vids, 16:9. Sizes in pt; a Google slide is 720 pt wide. Sized to be read from the back of a room (raised 1 Oct 2026: title 32, heading 18, body 16, small 14).

display.sample: Where does a coach's time go?

body.sample: Platforms, forms and rosters that need care every week.

docs.$description: Google Docs. Sizes and paragraph spacing (before, after) in pt; a Letter page is 612 pt wide. Heading 3 is the small label; running is the header and footer text.

subtitle.sample: A one-line summary of what this document is for.

body.sample: Technology serves people, not the other way around. Building systems that protect your time.

social.$description: LinkedIn posts, 1080 x 1080 px. Sizes in px. In the Google Slides post template the page is 11.25 in (810 pt), so 1 px = 0.75 pt.

statement.sample: Technology serves people, not the other way around.

spanish.sample: La tecnología está al servicio de las personas, y no al revés.

item.sample: One form that collects every request in one place

banner.$description: LinkedIn banner, 1584 x 396 px. Sizes in px. The profile photo covers the bottom left and phones trim the sides, so words sit in the middle third. LinkedIn shows it at about half size on a desktop, so these sizes read as 22, 13 and 9 px there.

line.sample: Building systems that protect your time.

spanish.sample: Construyendo sistemas que protegen tu tiempo.

web.$description: mrluisc.com. Sizes in px: size at the frame width (1200 px) and up, phoneSize at the phone width (375 px), growing smoothly in between. tracking is letter spacing in em, web only (Google's apps have none). measure is the longest line, in characters. Decided 2 Oct 2026.

display.sample: Where does a coach's time go?

lead.sample: Building systems that protect your time.

body.sample: Technology serves people, not the other way around. Platforms, forms and rosters that need care every week.

slides.note: Margins on every side of a 720 pt slide; the gap between columns.

docs.note: One inch, the Google Docs default.

motif.$description: The signature: a field of fine parallel lines and the dot that crosses it. Sizes are shares of the frame's width, so the motif keeps its proportions at any size.

title-slide.note: Field on the right; the dot's centre sits on the field's left edge.

content-slide.note: A narrow field on the right edge; a small dot low down.

doc-corner.note: First-page header art for documents. Shares of the page width (8.5 in): field about 0.75 in, dot 0.64 in, art 0.85 in tall; dot-y is a share of the art's height.

banner.note: LinkedIn banner. Field and dot are shares of the width (1584 px); dot-y is a share of the height.

mark.$description: The LC mark: one path drawn three times (a wide band, a see-through gap cut out of it, and a thin centre line). Geometry in the mark's own units; the view box is the mark's exact edges, so it centres cleanly anywhere. Built by mark/build_mark.py.
mark.clearSpaceNote: Keep empty space of at least a quarter of the mark's height on every side.
mark.minHeightNote: Below 32 px tall the three lines blur together: use the solid LC.

avatar.use: Avatars where a logo belongs: GitHub, a newsletter, a video channel. On LinkedIn, keep your photo.

lockup.name: Luis Carlos Moreno
lockup.note: Name size and gap are shares of the mark's height.

mark.refined: 1 Oct 2026: the L's foot lengthened from 22 to 28 units so the L stands steadier; the C kept its 120 degree opening, which reads as a C (narrower started to read as an O).

apps.$description: How Google's apps turn a line-spacing setting into the distance between lines. Every line value in these tokens is the distance you see, as a share of the type size (the web's line-height); the builders divide by the app's single spacing so Google draws exactly that.

google-slides.note: Google Slides puts single-spaced lines 1.2 x the type size apart, whatever the font (five titles and two body texts measured, 1 Oct 2026). Setting = line / 1.2.

google-docs.note: Google Docs puts single-spaced lines one lineBox apart (1.25 for Encode Sans). Setting = line / lineBox.
